text.p: Quality Houses Plc, hit by a huge glut of Bangkok residential condominiums and high mortgage rates, has switched to concentrate on building single detached houses.

"Some 13 percent of our two residential condominiums in Bangkok with a combined 580 units are still vacant," said Suwanna Wongsakulyong, Quality Houses assistant managing director told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
Suwanna said Bangkok now has about 43,000 residential condominium units, of which only 69 percent have been filled.
The Bangkok oversupply and 14-15 percent home mortgage rates have prompted the major Thai property developer to focus on the single detached house sector.

"There's a strong demand for single detached houses if prices are not too high, say at two to four million baht ($80,000-$160,000) per unit. Middle-income buyers can afford them. There's a bright prospect in this segment," said Suwanna.

She said the company is also looking for plots of land not too far from the Bangkok central business district to develop home office buildings to serve the high-end market with a unit price of over 20 million baht ($800,000), she said.
"It'll be very convenient for buyers who won't have to waste time commuting through Bangkok's busy traffic. We're trying to launch the project as soon as possible," Suwanna said.

The housing developer is planning to enter joint ventures to build serviced apartments in Burma and the Philippines, and to participate in another joint venture in building a hotel in Haiphong, Vietnam, she said.
"Right now our executives are negotiating with Burmese government officials. The negotiations began in early August," Suwanna said.
She was optimistic the talks on the Rangoon serviced apartment project would produce result soon. She said a project feasibility study was being conducted.
Quality Houses closed Thursday up 0.75 baht at 44.00.
